A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BALLAST study. Their main text, equations, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching v1 Appendices G–H to v2 Appendices H–I.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix G report original deployment simulations and ablations using synthetic Helmholtz fields and SUNTANS data.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix H retain the original deployment simulations and ablation results.

M1.justification: The implemented BALLAST procedure and its GP/SPDE sampler are retained, with the sampler renamed VaSE. Appendix G additionally specifies an extension to other half-integer Matérn smoothness values using higher-derivative states and describes handling irregular temporal grids.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic temporal Helmholtz fields and SUNTANS ocean-current data. Animal collars and meteorological balloons appear only as suggested applications in v2, not evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain UNIF, SOBOL, DIST-SEP, EIG, BALLAST-opt, and BALLAST-true. Comparator membership within the corresponding ablations is unchanged. Standard GP and SPDE sampling were already discussed comparatively in v1.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 changes the stated uniform initialization from all policies to all policies except SOBOL. This is a limited correction to the reported protocol; the appendix's Sobol construction remains unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish rerunning experiments. Other evaluation settings and metrics are retained.

E4.justification: The sample-number ablations, Monte Carlo versus full-stochasticity gaps, and projection-horizon study are retained in Figures 4 and 8–10. Moving these studies from Appendix G to H adds no new empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain two-standard-error reporting and the same repeated-run descriptions, including ten synthetic fields with ten runs each and 100 SUNTANS runs. The uncertainty displays are unchanged.

E6.justification: Section 4.1 adds illustrative computational cost estimates of approximately 10^8 for VaSE, 10^11 for SPDE, and 10^17 for standard GP. These are analytical estimates, not measured runtimes. Empirical plots and reported deployment savings of approximately 16% and 22% remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 adds the three-method complexity analysis in Appendix G.1 and Table 1 and revises cost expressions in B.1 and F.4. F.4 changes two spatial exponents from cubic to quadratic; its prediction bound now conflicts with the cubic dependence in Table 1/G.1. Existing propositions and proofs are retained.

C1.justification: V1 already claims the GP/SPDE sampler as a contribution. V2 foregrounds it as VaSE and strengthens the introduction's efficiency claim to thousands of times faster than SPDE and billions faster than standard GP. The principal BALLAST effectiveness claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly assumes negligible observation delay in Section 2.3 and adds animal-sensing and balloon-sensing applicability in the conclusion. It removes the proposed post-Bayesian response to model misspecification and reframes DIST-SEP's underperformance as unsurprising for an information-gain approximation.

D1.justification: Section 5 adds an experiment-code repository link. V1 already supplied the GPJax implementation-example link and detailed simulation, optimization, software, and hardware information; these details remain in v2 Appendix I.

R1.justification: V2 adds connections to spatio-temporal experimental design, entropy search, constrained sequential design, and other sensor applications. It removes the Laplante and Shen references and the explicit acknowledgment and citation of the stationary-field BALLAST workshop precursor, Zhang et al. (2024).

P1.justification: V2 reorders the background subsections, introduces a Problem Setup subsection, expands the EIG and sampling explanations, and reorganizes the conclusion. It also adds Appendix G and an Impact Statement. The overall narrative and most existing appendix text remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 1 and restyles Figure 3 with the VaSE label, revised arrows, and annotation colors. Typography, headers, and figure placement change, including separating Figures 8 and 9 across pages. The empirical plot graphics are retained unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 provides clearer sampler documentation, an explicit generalization, and code-access information. However, its stronger speed claims accompany inconsistent SPDE complexity bounds between Appendix F.4 and Table 1/G.1, and it removes acknowledgment of the BALLAST workshop precursor. With empirical evidence unchanged, these documentation gains and losses in consistency and attribution leave the net quality direction unclear.
